blogs.title: When Brain and Electrolytes Collide: SIADH as a Hidden Complication of Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s
blogs.description: This post dives into the pathophysiology and clinical clues that link central nervous system inflammation in Behçet’s disease to inappropriate ADH secretion. It reviews the diagnostic work‑up of hyponatraemia in an acutely ill patient, discusses how CNS cytokines (especially IL‑6) can drive SIADH, and highlights bedside signs—hiccups, rhabdomyolysis, and a normal MRI—that should alert clinicians to this masquerading electrolyte disorder.

blogs.title: Colchicine‑First? Rethinking the Role of Low‑Dose Colchicine in Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s
blogs.description: Here we question the dogma that corticosteroids are mandatory for neuro‑Behçet’s. By dissecting a case where colchicine monotherapy resolved mucocutaneous lesions, aseptic meningitis, and hyponatraemia, we explore colchicine’s anti‑inflammatory mechanisms (neutrophil inhibition, IL‑1β/IL‑6 suppression) and discuss when it can be safely considered a first‑line agent, especially for patients with steroid contraindications.

blogs.title: Beyond Brain Imaging: When a Normal MRI Fails to Rule Out Neuro‑Behçet’s
blogs.description: Many clinicians rely on MRI to confirm central nervous system involvement. This article examines the pitfalls of early MRI in acute neuro‑Behçet’s, illustrating how a normal scan can coexist with aseptic meningitis and significant CSF abnormalities. It covers alternative diagnostic strategies, including CSF analysis, neuro‑clinical features, and the timing of imaging.

blogs.title: Hyponatraemia in the Emergency Room: A Case‑Based Guide to SIADH in Infectious and Inflammatory Conditions
blogs.description: Focusing on the emergency department setting, this post reviews the algorithm for evaluating severe hyponatraemia, with an emphasis on SIADH secondary to CNS inflammation. It incorporates the presented case to highlight red flags (fasting hyponatraemia, low serum osmolality, euvolemic status) and practical management pearls—fluid restriction, monitoring, and cautious correction—while avoiding pitfalls like over‑administration of hypertonic saline.

blogs.title: The Silent ‘Other’ Symptoms of SIADH: Hiccups, Rhabdomyolysis, and Mis‑attributed Fatigue
blogs.description: Severe hyponatraemia can masquerade as other clinical problems. This piece discusses how hiccups, muscle weakness, and generalized malaise can be early manifestations of SIADH, especially in the context of meningitis or neuro‑inflammation. It offers a concise approach to discerning electrolyte‑driven symptoms from disease‑specific complaints.

blogs.title: Avoiding the ‘Lab Lure’: Targeted Investigations in Unexplained CNS Inflammation
blogs.description: With a broad differential for meningitis-like illness, clinicians often order extensive autoimmune panels or tumour markers. This article uses the case to illustrate a focused, exclusion‑based work‑up that avoids unnecessary tests, interprets non‑specific findings (e.g., mild sIL‑2R elevation), and balances the need for thoroughness with efficient resource use.
